title: Utilities and environmental approvals for a glass studio: city water and sewer, pretreatment, natural gas or propane, stormwater and land disturbance, and DEQ air permitting
question: What do I set up with the city and the utilities for a Staunton glass studio (water and sewer for the cold shop, natural gas or propane for the furnace, stormwater for any site work), and does a gas-fired glass furnace need an air permit from DEQ?
office: City of Staunton Public Works (water and sewer accounts) and its Engineering Division (new connections and facility fees); Community Development, Environmental Programs Division (erosion, stormwater and land disturbance); Columbia Gas of Virginia (natural gas); Virginia Department of Environmental Quality, Valley Regional Office (air permits and construction stormwater coverage)
summary: The city supplies water and sewer; electricity, gas and telecoms are private. Set up or transfer the water and sewer account with Public Works at 1911 Craigmont Road (540.332.3892); a business that needs a new or larger connection first files the Water and Sewer Connection and Facility Fees application with the City Engineer, because the fees (set by meter size: for the 2025-26 year a 5/8-inch meter paid $2,100 water and $3,100 sewer connection fees plus $3,500 and $6,850 facilities fees; a 3/4-inch meter $5,250 and $10,280 facilities fees; a 1-inch meter $8,750 and $17,130) must be settled before any building permit. Cold-working, grinding and polishing water goes to the city sewer, whose pretreatment chapter (City Code ch. 13.55) provides for wastewater surveys and permits for industrial users, so ask Public Works whether a glass shop's discharge needs a permit or a settling and solids trap. Natural gas comes from Columbia Gas of Virginia: start with its gas availability form (call back within two business days) or its New Business line (1-800-440-6111); a service line is installed within ten business days of site readiness and permits for small commercial service, and the house piping is the studio's licensed gas contractor's job under the city's gas permit. Propane instead means a tank or cylinders under the Fire Marshal's LP-gas permit and a city gas permit. Any site work disturbing more than 10,000 square feet needs a city land disturbing permit ($3,000 plus a $2,500-per-acre bond, after erosion and stormwater plan approval; an acre or more also needs DEQ construction general permit coverage). A gas-fired glass furnace, glory hole and kilns are fuel-burning equipment; DEQ's minor new source review exempts gaseous-fuel units below 50,000,000 Btu per hour and new sources whose uncontrolled emissions fall under the exemption rates (for example 25 tons a year of particulate matter, 40 of nitrogen oxides), but the owner must keep records showing the exemption and can ask the Valley Regional Office in Harrisonburg (540-574-7800) to confirm.

steps.step: Set up the city water and sewer account (or confirm the existing service and meter)
steps.who: Studio owner or landlord; Public Works Customer Service (1911 Craigmont Road; 540.332.3892; 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.)
steps.how: The city provides water and sewer; electricity (Dominion Energy or Shenandoah Valley Electric Cooperative), gas (Columbia Gas of Virginia) and telecoms are private. A property owner can set up the account by phone or at the Public Works office with the deed or settlement papers; a tenant must come in with the lease, photo ID and a $160 payment covering the deposit and processing (the page describes the residential process; ask about a commercial account and deposit). The minimum water charge is billed until service is terminated. Ask what meter serves the building; a cold shop with saws, lathes and polishing wheels and a cafe may need a larger meter, which changes the facilities fees in step 2.
steps.fee: Tenant deposit and processing $160 (residential page; commercial deposit not stated)
steps.quote: Step 1: Set up the account. Call the Public Works Department at 540.332.3892 or visit our office at 1911 Craigmont Road.

steps.step: For a new or larger connection, file the Water and Sewer Connection and Facility Fees application with the City Engineer before the building permit
steps.who: Property owner; Public Works, Engineering Division (City Hall, 3rd floor; 540.332.3858)
steps.how: Any new connection needs the application so the city can confirm service is available and set the fees; the building permit will not issue until it is done. Fees are based on water meter size, and the applicant agrees on the form to pay direct cost plus 30% if rock or other unusual conditions raise the installation cost. The schedule for July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026 (the newest copy archived) shows for a 5/8-inch meter a $2,100 water and $3,100 sewer connection fee (minimums) and $3,500 water and $6,850 sewer facilities fees, $15,550 in all; facilities fees rise with meter size (3/4-inch $5,250 water and $10,280 sewer; 1-inch $8,750 and $17,130; 1-1/2-inch $15,310 and $29,970; 2-inch $28,000 and $54,800). The form records a property class (business, residential or apartments) and whether sewer is charged. Ask for the current year's schedule.
steps.deadline: Before any building permit is issued
steps.fee: By meter size; 2025-26 schedule: 5/8-inch meter $15,550 total ($2,100 and $3,100 connection; $3,500 and $6,850 facilities); 3/4-inch facilities fees $5,250 water and $10,280 sewer; 1-inch $8,750 and $17,130
steps.quote: NOTE: The basis for all the above fees is the water meter size.

steps.step: Ask Public Works whether the cold shop's wastewater needs a pretreatment survey, permit or solids trap
steps.who: Studio owner; Public Works (540.332.3892); the city's pretreatment program under City Code ch. 13.55
steps.how: Grinding, cutting and polishing glass produces water carrying fine glass and abrasive solids and, for some processes, cerium or other compounds; sandblasting and acid etching add more. Staunton's sewer use and pretreatment chapter (City Code ch. 13.55, headings read on eCode360) sets prohibited discharge standards and specific pollutant limits, provides for a wastewater survey of users, and requires wastewater permits for industrial users, with sections on permitting new connections, application contents, duration, appeals and modification; its text was not read. Describe the processes and volumes to Public Works and ask whether the shop is a significant industrial user needing a permit, or whether a settling tank or solids interceptor on the cold-shop drain satisfies the ordinance. A cafe's grease goes through a grease interceptor sized in plan review; grease may never go to storm drains.
steps.deadline: Before the plumbing permit is final
steps.fee: Not stated on the pages read
steps.quote: Food vendors are not allowed to drain grease onto the site or into City storm drains, or leave grease at the site.

steps.step: Natural gas: check availability with Columbia Gas of Virginia and order service
steps.who: Studio owner or builder; Columbia Gas of Virginia (New Business 1-800-440-6111; emergencies 1-800-544-5606); the studio's licensed gas contractor; Building Services (gas permit)
steps.how: Fill in the natural gas availability form (choose commercial or industrial customer) and a representative calls back within two business days to say whether gas is available at the address; or call the New Business line to place an order for a new service line, a larger meter and service line for added load, or a conversion from another fuel. For a new service line the company's pledge is installation within ten business days once the site is ready and it has the necessary permits; the pledge covers residential and small commercial service only and not main extensions, so a hot shop's furnace and glory hole load should be discussed early with the New Business team, who may need the appliance inputs to size the meter. Private underground lines must be marked before construction and 811 called before any digging. The house piping from the meter to the furnace, glory hole and kilns is installed by your contractor under the city's gas permit (glass_studio_building_mechanical); the trade permit form asks for the gas type and whether appliances are vented. Columbia Gas also offers transportation service and business energy-efficiency programs.
steps.deadline: Order early; availability answer within two business days; line installed within ten business days of site readiness and permits for small commercial service
steps.fee: Not stated on the pages read; main extensions and larger services are priced by the company
steps.quote: Complete the simple gas availability form below, and we'll call you back within two business days to let you know if natural gas service is currently available at your home.

steps.step: Propane instead of (or alongside) natural gas: tank, Fire Marshal LP-gas permit and gas permit
steps.who: Studio owner; propane supplier; Fire Marshal's Office (540.332.3720); Building Services
steps.how: If natural gas is not available or the glory hole and torches run on propane, the tank or cylinder installation needs the city's gas permit (the trade form lists above-ground LP and in-ground LP; a storage tank installation is $200 per tank under § 15.10.120, read on eCode360) and the Fire Marshal's LP-gas operational permit ($50 a year; the exemption for small containers applies only to homes). Siting, separation from buildings and ignition sources, and cylinder exchange practices are inspected before the permit. See glass_studio_fire_permits.
steps.deadline: Before the tank is set or cylinders delivered
steps.fee: Fire Marshal LP-gas permit $50.00 a year (City Code § 15.25.055, read); city gas permit and storage tank permit $200.00 per tank (City Code § 15.10.120, read)
steps.quote: For the use and/or storage of LP Gas and Flammable/Combustible Liquids.

steps.step: Site work: land disturbing permit, erosion and stormwater plans, and DEQ construction permit coverage over an acre
steps.who: Studio owner or developer; Community Development, Environmental Programs Division (540.332.3858; StauntonStormwater@ci.staunton.va.us); DEQ
steps.how: An interior fit-out disturbs no land and needs none of this. New parking, a loading area, an addition or a new building that disturbs more than 10,000 square feet needs the city's Land Disturbing Permit ($3,000 plus an erosion and sediment control bond of $2,500 per whole acre, partial acres rounded up): submit the erosion and sediment control plan and stormwater management plan (with the site plan or VESMP plan through Planning & Zoning; $200 review, about 45 days), get them approved, apply in the online portal (ten business days), hold a pre-construction meeting, and have the city inspector approve the initial controls before any disturbance. Sites of an acre or more, or part of a larger common plan of development, also need DEQ's VSMP Construction General Permit, with a separate fee paid to DEQ. Sites under 10,000 square feet that are not single-family homes should ask the division what applies. State law requires the plan approval before any land-disturbing activity and gives the city 60 days to act on a plan.
steps.deadline: Before any land disturbance; city review ten business days after the plans are approved
steps.fee: Land disturbing permit $3,000; E&S bond $2,500 per whole acre; site plan or VESMP plan review $200; DEQ construction general permit fee paid to DEQ (amount not read)
steps.quote: E&S Bond: $2,500 per whole acre (cash/check/letter of credit). Please note partial acres are rounded up to the nearest whole acre.

steps.step: Air: work out whether the furnace, glory hole and kilns are exempt from a DEQ minor new source review permit, and keep the records
steps.who: Studio owner (with the equipment supplier's heat-input ratings); DEQ Valley Regional Office (4411 Early Rd., Harrisonburg, VA 22801; 540-574-7800)
steps.how: Virginia's minor new source review program applies to any new stationary source that emits regulated pollutants above the exemption thresholds in 9VAC5-80-1105; if a permit is needed it must be obtained before any work on the project starts. Two exemption tests apply together. By equipment type (subsection B): fuel burning equipment units are exempt when, in a single application, gaseous-fuel units have a maximum heat input under 50,000,000 Btu per hour (liquid fuel under 10,000,000), which a studio furnace, glory hole and kilns will be far below; whether a glass-melting furnace counts as fuel burning equipment or as a process unit is a question to put to DEQ. By emission rate (subsections C and D): a new source is exempt when its uncontrolled emissions (maximum rated capacity times an emission factor times 8,760 hours a year) are below every rate in the table, for example 100 tons a year of carbon monoxide, 40 of nitrogen oxides, 40 of sulfur dioxide and 25 of particulate matter, with separate toxic pollutant tests in subsection E. Any owner relying on an exemption must keep the records that show it, so file the furnace and burner ratings, fuel use and the calculation. DEQ's page invites facilities to ask the regional office whether they are exempt; Staunton is in the Valley Regional Office's area.
steps.deadline: Before installing the equipment, if a permit turns out to be required
steps.fee: None for an exempt source; DEQ application fees apply if a minor NSR permit is required (not read)
steps.quote: The facility may contact the appropriate DEQ regional office (i.e. the region where the facility is/will be located) for help in determining if you are exempt or need a minor NSR permit.

steps.who: Studio owner; Public Works Refuse & Recycling (540.332.3898)
steps.how: The city provides trash and recycling collection; ask Public Works about a commercial container, extra bag tags and whether broken glass and cullet can go to the recycling center or must be handled as trash. Hazardous shop waste (spent acids, solvents, cerium slurry) is not covered by the pages read; ask DEQ or a licensed hauler.
steps.fee: Not stated on the pages read
steps.quote: The Public Works Department provides responsive and essential services to sustain City infrastructure and keeps the City fully functional, from trash collection to street paving to water treatment.

The water and sewer fee schedule read covers July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026; the current application (639201513777370000) has no archive copy, so current-year amounts may differ. The Land Disturbing Permit application PDF also has no archive copy.

City Code ch. 13.55 (pretreatment) and ch. 13.01 (erosion and stormwater) were not read beyond their eCode360 headings, and eCode360's terms forbid quoting; whether a glass cold shop is an industrial user needing a wastewater permit, and the survey and application procedure, come from the chapter's section headings only.

DEQ's Air Permits page was read in an Internet Archive copy of 15 August 2025 because the live page refuses automated readers; the Valley Regional Office page is a July 2026 capture. The 9VAC5-80-1105 text was read live. Whether a glass-melting furnace is 'fuel burning equipment' (subsection B) or a process unit judged only by emission rate (subsections C to E), and the toxic-pollutant screening in subsection E, are DEQ determinations; this file does not calculate emissions.

Public Works' account set-up page describes homeowners and tenants; the commercial account process and deposit were not stated.
The special events page's grease rule is quoted as the city's clearest published statement on grease and storm drains; the sewer use ordinance's grease provisions were not read.
Staff names on the Engineering, Environmental Programs and Public Works pages and on the DEQ office page are omitted.
